need: put Windows 11 on a brand-new storage drive in a rebuilt desktop
clues: the new drive is blank and has no operating system
nothing on the old drive needs to be kept
the technician will answer each setup question at the computer
the owner wants no leftover settings from the old system
appliesWhen: the target drive or partition is blank or may be wiped, and nothing from an earlier OS must be kept
explanation: A clean install puts the operating system on an empty or wiped partition, so nothing from an older system carries over.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 30: Operating System Installations and Upgrades

need: move a Windows 10 workstation to Windows 11 while keeping its programs and files
clues: the PC already runs a licensed copy of Windows 10
the user's applications must still be there afterward
the hardware meets the Windows 11 requirements
the user's files have been backed up first
appliesWhen: an existing OS must move to a newer version and keep its applications and files
explanation: An in-place upgrade installs the newer version over the existing system and keeps applications, settings, and files. A backup is still made first, because an upgrade can fail.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 30: Operating System Installations and Upgrades

need: set up forty identical desktops with the same OS, apps, and settings in one afternoon
clues: the desktops are the same model with the same hardware
one reference computer is already fully configured
each copy will get a unique security identifier from Sysprep
each target drive is at least as large as the source drive
appliesWhen: many matching computers must receive a copy of one prepared system
explanation: Image deployment copies one prepared system to many computers, which works best when the hardware matches. Sysprep gives each copy its own security identifier so they do not conflict.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 30: Operating System Installations and Upgrades

need: give new laptops to remote staff without the IT team ever handling them
clues: the laptops ship from the reseller straight to each employee's home
each device enrolls in the company's Azure AD tenant on first sign-in
the company's apps download and install automatically
the employee only has to sign in
appliesWhen: new devices must be set up automatically from the supplier with no work by IT
explanation: In a zero-touch deployment, the supplier registers each device so that it enrolls in the organization's directory and pulls its configuration when the user first signs in.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 30: Operating System Installations and Upgrades; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 3: Windows Administration

need: return a store-bought laptop to the state it was in when it left the factory
clues: the laptop came from the maker with Windows preinstalled
the maker left a hidden section of the drive that holds a factory image
the user's data lives on a separate D: drive
no installation media came in the box
appliesWhen: a preinstalled computer must go back to its factory image from the maker's hidden copy
explanation: Computers with Windows preinstalled usually keep a factory image on a hidden section of the drive. Restoring from it reimages the system drive, and data stored on another drive is left alone.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 30: Operating System Installations and Upgrades

need: fix a Windows installation with damaged system files as a last resort
clues: other repairs have already failed
the user's files and applications must not be lost
the hardware is working normally
the same version of Windows will be put back in place
appliesWhen: the existing OS is damaged and must be reinstalled while keeping files and applications
explanation: A repair installation reinstalls the same version of Windows over itself and keeps files and applications. In Windows 11, Reset PC with Keep my files does a similar repair.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 30: Operating System Installations and Upgrades

need: install Linux on a single PC that has no optical drive and no network installation server
clues: the technician has downloaded the ISO file
a tool such as Rufus can make removable media bootable
the firmware boot order can be changed to boot from removable media
it is one computer, not a fleet
appliesWhen: a single computer must boot installation files copied from an ISO onto removable media
explanation: The most common local installation copies the ISO onto a bootable flash drive and sets the firmware to boot from it first.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 30: Operating System Installations and Upgrades

need: start Windows installations on twenty lab computers from a server, with no media in the computers
clues: the network adapters support the Preboot Execution Environment
a deployment server holds the installation files
the same network has DHCP and TFTP services
no flash drives or discs may be used
appliesWhen: a PXE-compliant computer must boot from the network and pull its installation files from a server
explanation: A PXE-capable adapter lets a computer boot from the network, find the DHCP server, and load the installation from a deployment server such as MDT or MECM.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 30: Operating System Installations and Upgrades

need: install a second operating system from installation files that are already stored inside the computer
clues: the files sit on a separate partition of the storage drive
there is no USB port free and no network server
the source of the files must be a different place from the target of the install
the owner wants a boot menu to choose the OS later
appliesWhen: the installation files are stored on a separate partition or drive inside the computer
explanation: An OS can be installed from fixed media in the computer, as long as the files are on a different partition or drive than the target. With two operating systems, a boot menu lets the user pick one at startup.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 30: Operating System Installations and Upgrades

need: install a server OS straight from the vendor's site onto a bare-metal cloud host
clues: the host has no local media at all
the vendor offers automated provisioning online
the installation files come from the vendor's servers, not the local network
the host has a fast connection to the outside
appliesWhen: the OS files are delivered from the vendor over the Internet
explanation: Some operating systems, such as Ubuntu Server, can be provisioned directly over the Internet with no local media or local server.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 30: Operating System Installations and Upgrades

need: set up the partition table on a new 6 TB drive in a UEFI computer
clues: the drive is far larger than 2 TB
the firmware runs in UEFI mode
the owner may want more than four partitions
the partition table should be stored in more than one place
appliesWhen: the drive is larger than 2 TB or needs more than four partitions on a UEFI system
explanation: GPT allows up to 128 partitions and partitions far larger than 2 TB, and it keeps copies of its partition table. It is part of the UEFI standard.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 30: Operating System Installations and Upgrades

need: prepare a small boot drive for an old computer whose firmware is legacy BIOS only
clues: the motherboard has no UEFI support
the drive is 500 GB
two partitions are enough
the system must boot the old way from the first sector
appliesWhen: a legacy BIOS system boots a drive of 2 TB or less with four or fewer primary partitions
explanation: MBR is the older scheme that legacy BIOS systems boot from. It limits partitions to 2 TB and four primary partitions, which is fine for a small drive.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 30: Operating System Installations and Upgrades

need: make one volume that stretches across two physical drives
clues: the two drives are installed in the same Windows PC
the volume must be resized later without reformatting
the data has been backed up before the change
the change will be made in Disk Management
appliesWhen: volumes must span, stripe, or mirror across drives or be resized
explanation: Basic disks hold only simple partitions. Converting to a dynamic disk allows spanned, striped, mirrored, and RAID 5 volumes and lets volumes be resized.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 30: Operating System Installations and Upgrades; CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 33: Microsoft Operating System Features and Tools, Part II

need: create six separate drive letters on one drive that must keep its older partition style
clues: the drive uses MBR and cannot be converted
the partition table allows at most four primary partitions
three primary partitions already exist
each section needs its own drive letter
appliesWhen: an MBR disk needs more than four sections
explanation: On an MBR disk, one of the four partition slots can be an extended partition, which is divided into logical drives that each get a letter.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 30: Operating System Installations and Upgrades

need: format the main partition where Windows 11 will be installed
clues: the volume needs file permissions and auditing
encryption, compression, and disk quotas may be used
it is the default the Windows installer chooses
the partition will be at least 64 GB
appliesWhen: a Windows system volume or internal drive needs security, quotas, and large file support
explanation: NTFS is the file system Windows installs to by default and supports file security, encryption, compression, and quotas.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 2: Windows Configuration; CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 30: Operating System Installations and Upgrades

need: format a 256 GB flash drive that moves large video files between a Windows PC and a Mac
clues: some single files are larger than 4 GB
both macOS and Windows must read and write the drive
it is removable flash storage
file permissions are not needed
appliesWhen: a large removable flash drive must hold big files and work across operating systems
explanation: exFAT was made for large flash drives and is read and written by Windows and macOS. It has no 4 GB file limit, which FAT32 has.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 2: Windows Configuration

need: format a small 16 GB memory stick for an older device that reads only a basic file system
clues: the device does not understand NTFS or exFAT
every file on the stick is smaller than 4 GB
the stick is small
older operating systems must also read it
appliesWhen: a small drive must be read by older devices and operating systems
explanation: FAT32 is the old, widely supported file system that almost any device can read. Its limits do not matter on a small stick with small files.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 2: Windows Configuration

need: format a large data volume on a Windows server that must detect and repair data corruption by itself
clues: the volume holds many terabytes of project data
the system should scan for hidden damage on its own
data integrity matters more than booting from it
it is not a removable drive
appliesWhen: a large Windows data volume needs built-in integrity checks and self-repair
explanation: ReFS is a Microsoft file system built for availability, scale, and integrity. It checks data for corruption and fixes it.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 2: Windows Configuration

clues: the installer shows no drive to install to
the computer has a brand-new NVMe drive
the drive is detected in the UEFI setup
the installation media boots normally

answer.cause: Windows Setup has no driver for the new storage controller
answer.action: Load the manufacturer's storage driver during setup

firstStep: Check the drive maker's website for a storage driver for Windows
appliesWhen: a new or uncommon storage drive is not seen by the installer
explanation: Newer storage hardware may not be recognized by the installer. Supplying the maker's third-party driver lets Setup see the drive.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 30: Operating System Installations and Upgrades

clues: the scanner stopped working right after the Windows 11 upgrade
the scanner shows a yellow triangle in Device Manager
the scanner still works on another computer
the scanner is several years old

answer.cause: the device has no driver for the new operating system
answer.action: Install a driver for the new OS from the device maker

firstStep: Check the device maker's website for a driver for the new OS
appliesWhen: older hardware has no working driver for the newer OS
explanation: Before an upgrade, every device needs a driver for the new OS. Without one, Windows shows the device in a problem state.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 30: Operating System Installations and Upgrades; CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 32: Microsoft Operating System Features and Tools, Part I

clues: an old accounting program will not start after the upgrade
every other application runs normally
the program worked on the previous Windows version
the vendor has released a newer version of the program

answer.cause: the application is not compatible with the new OS
answer.action: Install the vendor's version of the application that supports the new OS

firstStep: Check the vendor's compatibility information for the new OS
appliesWhen: an application written for the older OS does not run on the new one
explanation: Application support must be checked before an upgrade. A program made for the older version may not run on the newer one until the vendor updates it.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 30: Operating System Installations and Upgrades

clues: the Windows 11 upgrade will not start
the upgrade check says the PC does not meet the requirements
the PC is eight years old with no TPM 2.0
the PC runs Windows 10 normally

answer.cause: the hardware does not meet the minimum requirements of the new OS
answer.action: Replace the computer or upgrade the parts that do not meet the requirements

firstStep: Compare the PC's hardware with the Windows 11 minimum requirements
appliesWhen: the computer does not meet the minimum hardware requirements of the new OS
explanation: Windows 11 has hardware requirements, such as TPM 2.0 and UEFI, that older computers may not meet. The hardware must be checked against them before an upgrade.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 30: Operating System Installations and Upgrades; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 1: Operating System Basics

clues: the PC no longer receives security updates
the PC still runs Windows 10 Pro in late 2026
the support end date for that version has passed
the hardware is new enough for Windows 11

answer.cause: the OS version has reached the end of its support life cycle
answer.action: Upgrade the computer to a supported version of Windows

firstStep: Check Microsoft's life-cycle date for the installed version
appliesWhen: the installed OS version is past its end-of-support date
explanation: Once a version reaches the end of its product life cycle, Microsoft stops sending security and feature updates. Windows 10 Home and Pro support ended on October 14, 2025.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 30: Operating System Installations and Upgrades; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 1: Operating System Basics

task: upgrading a user's Windows 10 computer to Windows 11

steps.do: Check that the hardware meets the Windows 11 requirements
steps.done: checked that the hardware meets the Windows 11 requirements

steps.do: Confirm that the applications and drivers support Windows 11
steps.done: confirmed that the applications and drivers support Windows 11

steps.do: Back up the user's files and preferences
steps.done: backed up the user's files and preferences

steps.do: Install any missing drivers and Windows updates
steps.done: installed any missing drivers and Windows updates

steps.do: Have the user confirm that the files and applications work
steps.done: had the user confirm that the files and applications work

explanation: An upgrade is planned first: hardware, then application and driver support, then a backup of the files and preferences. Only then is the upgrade run and the result checked.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 30: Operating System Installations and Upgrades

need: close a frozen program that is using almost all of the processor right now
clues: the program window has stopped responding
the user cannot close it with the X button
the user wants to see the live CPU and memory use of each program
a restart is not wanted
appliesWhen: a running process must be viewed live or ended, or a startup app or signed-in user must be managed
explanation: Task Manager shows each process's live CPU and memory use, and End task stops a process that is hoarding resources.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 32: Microsoft Operating System Features and Tools, Part I

need: free the memory held by a remote user who disconnected instead of signing off
clues: the user's session shows as Disconnected
the user's programs are still open in that session
the technician wants to sign the session off from the local desktop
a quick Ctrl+Shift+Esc tool is preferred
appliesWhen: a running process must be viewed live or ended, or a startup app or signed-in user must be managed
explanation: The Users tab of Task Manager lists each signed-in user and their resource use, and it can sign off a disconnected session.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 32: Microsoft Operating System Features and Tools, Part I

need: find out why a program has been crashing every few days
clues: the crashes leave no message on screen
the technician wants the error entries and their event IDs
the System and Application logs should be checked
the logs show information, warning, and error entries
appliesWhen: past errors, warnings, or audit events in the Windows logs must be read
explanation: Event Viewer keeps the System, Application, and Security logs, with information, warning, error, and audit entries. An application error entry shows which program faulted and its event ID.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 32: Microsoft Operating System Features and Tools, Part I

need: make a newly installed second drive usable in File Explorer
clues: the new drive does not appear in File Explorer
it must be initialized and given a volume
a graphical tool is preferred over the command line
the volume needs a drive letter and NTFS
appliesWhen: drives must be initialized, partitioned, formatted, or given letters
explanation: Disk Management initializes new drives, creates and formats volumes, assigns drive letters, and converts disks to dynamic.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 33: Microsoft Operating System Features and Tools, Part II

need: run a disk check script automatically every Sunday at 2 a.m.
clues: nobody will be at the computer when it runs
the job must repeat every week
a trigger and an action must be set
built-in tasks in the library can be reused
appliesWhen: a program or action must run automatically at set times or on a trigger
explanation: Task Scheduler runs programs or actions at set times or when a trigger happens, and its library holds built-in tasks.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 32: Microsoft Operating System Features and Tools, Part I

need: go back to the previous version of a video driver after an update made the screen flicker
clues: the flicker started right after the driver update
the older driver version worked well
the device shows a yellow triangle
the Driver tab of the device's properties is needed
appliesWhen: a device's driver must be updated, rolled back, or the device enabled or disabled
explanation: Device Manager lists every device and can update, roll back, disable, or uninstall its driver. Roll Back Driver returns to the version that worked.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 32: Microsoft Operating System Features and Tools, Part I

need: check when a security certificate the user's web app relies on expires
clues: the app warns about a certificate problem
the technician wants to see the issuer and expiry date
the certificates are stored for the current user
the console is opened from Run
appliesWhen: the installed security certificates must be viewed or managed
explanation: Certificate Manager lists the certificates installed in Windows, with each one's issuer, uses, and expiration date.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 32: Microsoft Operating System Features and Tools, Part I

need: add a local account to the built-in Backup Operators group
clues: the computer is not joined to a domain
the Settings app cannot assign that built-in group
the technician may also reset the account's password
the change applies only to this computer
appliesWhen: local user accounts and group memberships need detailed control
explanation: Local Users and Groups gives more control than Settings over local accounts: it creates users, resets passwords, and manages groups such as Backup Operators.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 32: Microsoft Operating System Features and Tools, Part I

need: record processor, memory, and network adapter use over a whole workday for later review
clues: the slowdown happens only at certain hours
the data must be logged and saved
specific counters for several objects must be added
a report view will be shown to the manager
appliesWhen: chosen counters must be tracked over time and logged for later review
explanation: Performance Monitor tracks objects with counters on real-time graphs and can log the data for later viewing, which Task Manager and Resource Monitor cannot.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 32: Microsoft Operating System Features and Tools, Part I

need: set a rule that hides the Control Panel from every user of a standalone Pro workstation
clues: the computer is not in a domain
the rule is under User Configuration, Administrative Templates
the change must be made through a policy, not by editing settings by hand
the edition is Windows 11 Pro
appliesWhen: rules for the computer or its users must be set through local policy
explanation: The Local Group Policy Editor sets Computer Configuration and User Configuration rules, including hundreds of Administrative Templates settings.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 32: Microsoft Operating System Features and Tools, Part I

need: list the exact hardware resources, components, and software environment of a PC without changing anything
clues: the vendor support line asks for a full system summary
nothing may be changed on the computer
the details can also be read from a remote computer
the BIOS version and installed RAM must be reported
appliesWhen: a read-only summary of hardware, components, and software is needed
explanation: System Information shows a summary of hardware resources, components, and the software environment, but it cannot change anything.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 33: Microsoft Operating System Features and Tools, Part II

need: see which processes are reading and writing the disk and using the network right now
clues: the technician wants more detail than Task Manager gives
a full counter setup would take too long
the CPU, Disk, Network, and Memory sections should be on one screen
process IDs must be shown
appliesWhen: live per-process use of the CPU, disk, network, and memory is needed in more detail than Task Manager
explanation: Resource Monitor shows live CPU, disk, network, and memory use for each process. It gives more detail than Task Manager without the setup of Performance Monitor.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 33: Microsoft Operating System Features and Tools, Part II

need: boot the computer in Safe boot on the next restarts while troubleshooting a failing service
clues: the computer starts normally now
a diagnostic or selective startup may also be tried
services must be disabled quickly for testing
the setting must be set back to Normal startup afterward
appliesWhen: the startup mode, boot options, or services must be changed for troubleshooting
explanation: System Configuration sets diagnostic or selective startup, Safe boot and other boot options, and enables or disables services for testing.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 33: Microsoft Operating System Features and Tools, Part II

need: free space on a nearly full C: drive by removing temporary files and old Windows update files
clues: the Recycle Bin and temporary Internet files take up space
system files from Windows Update can be removed too
no user documents may be deleted
the company policy asks for this monthly
appliesWhen: temporary and leftover files must be removed to free drive space
explanation: Disk Cleanup removes temporary files, the Recycle Bin, and, with Clean up system files, old Windows Update files.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 33: Microsoft Operating System Features and Tools, Part II

need: speed up an old mechanical hard drive whose files are scattered across the platters
clues: the drive LED shows constant activity
the drive is an HDD, not an SSD
the job can run off-hours and be scheduled
files have been written and erased for years
appliesWhen: a mechanical drive must be analyzed and made contiguous again
explanation: Optimize Drives (Disk Defragment) rearranges a fragmented hard disk so files are contiguous again, which cuts wear and speeds access.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 33: Microsoft Operating System Features and Tools, Part II

need: change a Windows setting that has no option in Settings, Control Panel, or the command line
clues: the vendor's guide names a key under HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE
a DWORD value must be changed
a backup should be made before any change
the setting is stored in a hive
appliesWhen: a setting must be changed directly in the database of Windows settings
explanation: The Registry Editor edits the keys and values in the Windows settings database. Back it up before a change.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 33: Microsoft Operating System Features and Tools, Part II

clues: the PC starts in Safe Mode on every restart
a technician troubleshot the PC last week
the screen shows Safe Mode in each corner
no errors appear in startup

answer.cause: Safe boot was left on in System Configuration
answer.action: Set System Configuration back to Normal startup and clear Safe boot

firstStep: Open System Configuration and look at the Boot tab
appliesWhen: the boot settings were changed for troubleshooting and never reset
explanation: Safe boot set on the Boot tab of System Configuration stays on for every restart. It must be reset to Normal startup after troubleshooting.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 33: Microsoft Operating System Features and Tools, Part II

clues: the PC takes several minutes to become usable after sign-in
many tray icons appear at startup
the slowness goes away after a few minutes
the hardware passes its tests

answer.cause: too many high-impact apps launch at startup
answer.action: Disable the unneeded apps on the Startup apps tab of Task Manager

firstStep: Check the startup impact column in Task Manager
appliesWhen: many apps are set to launch at every startup
explanation: Every enabled startup app runs at sign-in, and high-impact ones slow the start. Disabling them in Task Manager keeps them from launching.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 32: Microsoft Operating System Features and Tools, Part I

clues: the shared PC is low on memory
a remote worker used it through Remote Desktop yesterday
the remote worker closed the window without signing out
the remote worker's programs are still listed as running

answer.cause: a disconnected session is still holding its programs open
answer.action: Sign off the disconnected user from the Users tab of Task Manager

firstStep: Check the Users tab of Task Manager for other sessions
appliesWhen: a remote user disconnected instead of signing off
explanation: Disconnecting leaves a session's programs open, so they keep using memory. Signing the user off closes them and frees the resources.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 32: Microsoft Operating System Features and Tools, Part I

need: move the prompt from its current folder to a different folder on the same volume
clues: the prompt opened in the wrong folder
a script must be run from inside the target folder
nothing in either folder should be listed, created, or removed
going up one level or back to the root of the volume should also be possible
appliesWhen: the prompt's working folder must change to another location
explanation: The cd command changes the current working directory. The cd .. form moves up to the parent folder and cd \ jumps to the root of the volume.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 34: Microsoft Command-Line Tools, Part I

need: list the files and subfolders that a folder holds from the prompt
clues: the user only wants to see what the folder contains
the output should pause one screen at a time
a wide list layout would also help
nothing may be moved, copied, or deleted
appliesWhen: the contents of a folder must be listed at the prompt
explanation: The dir command shows the contents of the current folder or of any path given to it. Switches such as /p (one page at a time) and /w (wide list) change how the list is shown.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 34: Microsoft Command-Line Tools, Part I

need: see the IP address, subnet mask, and default gateway that the PC is using
clues: the user says the PC cannot reach any websites
the technician wants to know whether the address came from DHCP or APIPA
the MAC address of the adapter and the DNS server address are also needed
the cached DNS entries may need to be cleared afterward
appliesWhen: the PC's own TCP/IP settings must be shown, released, renewed, or its DNS cache flushed
explanation: The ipconfig command shows the current TCP/IP settings of each adapter, and the /all switch adds the MAC address, DHCP status, and DNS servers. It is one of the first tools to use for a connectivity problem.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 35: Microsoft Command-Line Tools, Part II

need: check whether the file server answers over the network
clues: the server has a known IP address
the round-trip time of each reply should be shown
the test should repeat until the technician presses Ctrl+C
the technician will unplug and replug cables while the test runs
appliesWhen: the technician only needs to know whether one host replies and how fast
explanation: The ping command sends test packets to a host and reports each reply and its round-trip time. The -t switch keeps it running until it is stopped, which helps when testing cables and ports.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 35: Microsoft Command-Line Tools, Part II

need: list the active TCP sessions between the PC and remote hosts
clues: the local and foreign address of each session must be shown
the port used by each connection is needed
the program behind each session should be listed too
the results should be shown in numeric form
appliesWhen: the PC's current network sessions and their ports must be listed
explanation: The netstat command shows the network statistics and the sessions that the local computer has with remote hosts. Its -an switches show TCP and UDP in numeric form, and -nab adds the executable for each session.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 35: Microsoft Command-Line Tools, Part II

need: find out which IP addresses a domain name resolves to
clues: websites load by IP address but not by name
the DNS server must be queried directly
both the IPv4 and the IPv6 address records are needed
an interactive shell for more DNS queries would help
appliesWhen: a DNS server must be queried for the records of a name
explanation: The nslookup command (name server lookup) queries DNS servers and returns the addresses and other records for a name. Typed alone, it opens a shell for further DNS queries.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 35: Microsoft Command-Line Tools, Part II

need: map a drive letter to a shared folder on another computer
clues: the share is reached by its UNC path
the user wants the share to appear as drive F:
the work must be done at the prompt
a list of the drives already mapped should also be shown
appliesWhen: a drive letter must be mapped to a network share or the mapped drives listed
explanation: The net use command lists the mapped network drives and maps a new one with the form x: \\computername\sharename. It can also connect to hidden shares whose names end in $.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 35: Microsoft Command-Line Tools, Part II

need: find the router along the path to a remote site where traffic stops
clues: the remote site cannot be reached but the default gateway answers
each hop should be listed with three timings
a quick list of hops is enough without packet loss statistics
names along the way may be skipped with the /d switch for speed
appliesWhen: each router on the path must be listed quickly with its response times
explanation: The tracert command pings each router between the PC and the destination and lists every hop with three timings. A trace that stops or shows asterisks points to the router where the problem is.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 35: Microsoft Command-Line Tools, Part II

need: measure the latency and packet loss at each router between the PC and a remote server
clues: the link to the server is slow only at times
the statistics for every hop should be computed at the end
the technician can wait for a longer test
a plain list of hops is not enough
appliesWhen: latency and packet loss must be measured for every hop on the path
explanation: The pathping command lists the same hops as tracert and then computes the latency and packet loss between the source and each router. It takes longer to run but gives statistics for every hop.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 35: Microsoft Command-Line Tools, Part II

need: find and fix file system errors and bad sectors on a drive
clues: the PC shows a missing operating system message at boot
the boot order in the firmware is already correct
the technician can open a prompt from Windows RE
a status report of the drive should be shown
appliesWhen: the drive's file system must be checked and repaired
explanation: The chkdsk command checks a drive and reports its status; /F fixes errors and /R locates bad sectors and recovers readable data. It can be run from Windows RE when the system will not boot.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 34: Microsoft Command-Line Tools, Part I

need: prepare a USB flash drive with a new NTFS file system at the prompt
clues: the data on the flash drive is no longer needed
the drive already has one partition
the file system type must be set with the /FS switch
the drive appears as F: in File Explorer
appliesWhen: a volume must be given a new file system and its old data erased
explanation: The format command writes a new file system such as NTFS, FAT, or FAT32 to a volume. The /FS switch sets the file system type.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 34: Microsoft Command-Line Tools, Part I

need: create, extend, and assign drive letters to volumes without the graphical disk console
clues: the technician is at a text-only prompt
a new partition must be created and made active
the same work is normally done in Disk Management
a drive letter must be given to a new volume
appliesWhen: partitions and volumes must be created, deleted, extended, or given letters at the prompt
explanation: The diskpart utility is the command-line counterpart of Disk Management. From its own prompt it creates, deletes, and extends volumes, assigns drive letters, and marks a partition active.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 34: Microsoft Command-Line Tools, Part I

need: create a new folder named Reports inside an existing folder at the prompt
clues: the Reports folder does not exist yet
no files need to be copied into it yet
the full path to the parent folder is known
the current working folder must stay the same
appliesWhen: a new folder must be created
explanation: The md command (make directory, also mkdir) creates a folder at the path given. It can create a folder anywhere in the tree without changing the current location.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 34: Microsoft Command-Line Tools, Part I

need: delete an old project folder and everything inside it at the prompt
clues: the folder is no longer needed
the folder still holds files and subfolders
the /S switch can be added to include its contents
the parent folder must be kept
appliesWhen: a folder must be removed
explanation: The rmdir command (also rd) removes a folder, and its /S switch removes a folder that still holds files. It deletes the folder rather than moving or copying it.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 34: Microsoft Command-Line Tools, Part I

need: replicate a large folder tree with all its subfolders to a share on another computer
clues: the network link sometimes drops during long transfers
the file timestamps and attributes must be kept
the destination should mirror the whole source tree
the destination is given as a UNC path
appliesWhen: whole folder trees must be copied or mirrored, even over an unreliable network
explanation: The robocopy command (Robust File Copy) replicates folders and their contents, tolerates network interruptions, and keeps attributes and timestamps. It is the successor to xcopy and can mirror a whole tree to another computer.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 34: Microsoft Command-Line Tools, Part I

need: display the name of the local computer
clues: the technician is on the phone with the user
the name is needed to find the PC in the asset list
the name does not need to be changed
a single short command is easiest for the user to type
appliesWhen: only the local computer's name must be shown
explanation: The hostname command prints the name of the local computer. It cannot change the name, which is done in the GUI or with rename-computer in PowerShell.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 35: Microsoft Command-Line Tools, Part II

need: list the local accounts and add a new standard account at the prompt
clues: the prompt is running as an administrator
the new account must not be an administrator
an old account must be turned off with the /active switch
an unused account must be removed with /delete
appliesWhen: local user accounts must be listed, added, turned on or off, or deleted
explanation: Typed alone, net user lists the user accounts on the local computer. Its /add option creates a standard account, /active turns an account on or off, and /delete removes it.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 35: Microsoft Command-Line Tools, Part II

need: find out which edition, version, and build of Windows the PC is running
clues: a new app needs version 24H2 or later
a window that also shows the licensing information is enough
the user can start it from the Run box or the Search tool
nothing on the PC must change
appliesWhen: the Windows edition, version, and build number must be shown
explanation: The winver command opens a window that shows the Windows edition, version, and build number, plus trademark and licensing information. It runs from the command line, the Run box, or Search.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 34: Microsoft Command-Line Tools, Part I

need: confirm which user account and privileges the current session is using
clues: the technician is working on a remote device
the user's group memberships must also be listed
the domain of the signed-in account is needed
the /all switch can show every detail
appliesWhen: the signed-in user's name, domain, groups, and privileges must be shown
explanation: The whoami command shows the domain and username of the current user, and /all adds the groups, privileges, and other permission details. It confirms which account the technician is working as.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 35: Microsoft Command-Line Tools, Part II

need: see the switches and the syntax that a tool accepts before running it
clues: the technician does not remember the right switch
no internet access is available for online documentation
the help text should show in the prompt itself
the same method should work for every tool at the prompt
appliesWhen: the help text and switches of a tool must be shown
explanation: Adding /? after any command at the prompt shows its help file, with the syntax and every switch. It works for all commands, while help followed by a name works only for some.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 34: Microsoft Command-Line Tools, Part I

need: apply changed policies on a PC without the user signing out and back in
clues: the change was made in the Local Group Policy Editor
the new password rules must take effect now
the PC runs Windows 11 Pro
the same update may be run against a remote system
appliesWhen: modified policies must be applied right away
explanation: The gpupdate command applies every policy that has changed on the target computer without a sign-out. It can be run on the local PC or against a remote system.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 34: Microsoft Command-Line Tools, Part I

need: see which policies are applied to a user and computer
clues: a policy does not seem to take effect on a PC
the Resultant Set of Policy should be shown
the report should be saved as an HTML file
the target may be a remote computer named with /S
appliesWhen: the policies in effect for a user and computer must be reported
explanation: The gpresult command shows the Resultant Set of Policy (RSoP) for a user and computer, and /R gives a short summary. The /S switch targets a remote system, and /H or /X saves the report.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 34: Microsoft Command-Line Tools, Part I

need: scan the protected Windows system files and replace any that are missing or corrupt
clues: the Edge browser and other Windows apps crash
the drive itself passed a disk check
the details of each repair should be written to CBS.log
the scan should start right away
appliesWhen: protected system files must be checked and repaired
explanation: System File Checker scans protected system files and replaces wrong or missing ones; sfc /scannow scans and repairs at once. It writes each repair to CBS.log in %systemroot%\Logs\CBS.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 34: Microsoft Command-Line Tools, Part I

need: set a proxy server and a trusted site zone for an old web app that runs in IE mode
clues: the proxy is entered under LAN settings on the Connections tab
the company portal must be added to the trusted sites zone
the classic dialog opens with inetcpl.cpl
appliesWhen: the change is to the home page, security zones, certificates, or proxy settings used by Internet Explorer and IE mode
explanation: Internet Options opens the Internet Properties dialog, which holds the security zones on one tab and the proxy settings on the Connections tab. These settings apply to Internet Explorer and IE mode in Edge, and the proxy setting can also affect other apps that use the IE engine.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 36: Windows Control Panel Utilities

need: import a site certificate and turn off AutoComplete for pages opened in IE mode
clues: the certificate list is on the Content tab
the pop-up blocker on the Privacy tab must also be checked
the legacy browser settings are the ones that must change
appliesWhen: the change is to the home page, security zones, certificates, or proxy settings used by Internet Explorer and IE mode
explanation: The Content tab of Internet Options lists the installed certificates, imports new ones, and controls AutoComplete. The Privacy tab of the same dialog holds the pop-up blocker.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 36: Windows Control Panel Utilities

need: share an older USB printer with the other computers in the office
clues: the printer has no network port of its own
printer sharing is already turned on in the advanced sharing settings
the share name is set on the Sharing tab of the printer properties
appliesWhen: printers or other attached devices must be added, configured, shared, or removed from one Control Panel window
explanation: Devices and Printers is where printers and other attached devices are added, configured, and removed. Right-clicking a printer there opens its properties, and the Sharing tab shares it with the network.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 38: Windows Networking

need: remove an old printer and add a new one from the classic Control Panel view
clues: the old printer was replaced last week
the help desk script still uses Control Panel
in Windows 11 the link may open the modern printers page
appliesWhen: printers or other attached devices must be added, configured, shared, or removed from one Control Panel window
explanation: Devices and Printers adds, configures, troubleshoots, and removes printers and other devices. In Windows 11 the applet hands off to the Bluetooth & devices page in Settings.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 36: Windows Control Panel Utilities

need: turn on Hyper-V on a Windows Pro workstation
clues: the feature ships with Windows but is off by default
the technician opens the applet with appwiz.cpl
the same window can also repair or uninstall desktop software
appliesWhen: a desktop program must be repaired or uninstalled, installed updates viewed, or a Windows feature turned on or off
explanation: Programs and Features has the Turn Windows features on or off link, where features such as Hyper-V and the .NET Framework are added. It also repairs and uninstalls programs.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 36: Windows Control Panel Utilities

need: repair a desktop program whose files were damaged
clues: the program is still in the classic installed list
the program offers Change and Repair buttons
the user also wants to view the installed Windows updates
appliesWhen: a desktop program must be repaired or uninstalled, installed updates viewed, or a Windows feature turned on or off
explanation: Programs and Features lists the installed programs with options to change, repair, or uninstall them. It also links to the list of installed updates.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 36: Windows Control Panel Utilities

need: turn on network discovery and file and printer sharing for the private profile
clues: the change is made under Change advanced sharing settings
the technician also wants the classic adapter view
the PC must show which network profile it is in
appliesWhen: the network profile, discovery and sharing options, adapter settings, or a new connection must be set from the classic network window
explanation: Network and Sharing Center shows the active connections and their network profile. Its Change advanced sharing settings link turns network discovery and file and printer sharing on or off for each profile.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 38: Windows Networking

need: build a new VPN connection with the classic wizard
clues: the wizard link reads Set up a new connection or network
the technician also wants to see the active connections
the Change adapter settings link must be close by
appliesWhen: the network profile, discovery and sharing options, adapter settings, or a new connection must be set from the classic network window
explanation: Network and Sharing Center has the Set up a new connection or network wizard and the Change adapter settings link. It also displays each active connection and its profile.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 38: Windows Networking

need: change the paging file size and allow Remote Desktop connections
clues: the Advanced tab holds the performance and virtual memory options
the Remote tab must also be changed
the classic properties dialog opens with sysdm.cpl
appliesWhen: the computer name, virtual memory and performance, restore points, or remote connection settings in System Properties must be changed
explanation: The System applet opens the About page, and its advanced link opens System Properties (sysdm.cpl). That dialog holds the computer name, performance and virtual memory, remote settings, and restore point options.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Core 2 Chapter 2: Windows Configuration

need: turn on restore point creation for drive C before a risky change
clues: the option is on the Protection tab of the classic properties dialog
the same dialog also renames the computer
the user wants the Control Panel route
appliesWhen: the computer name, virtual memory and performance, restore points, or remote connection settings in System Properties must be changed
explanation: The System applet leads to System Properties, whose Protection tab turns restore points on for a drive and creates one. The same dialog also changes the computer name and domain or workgroup.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Core 2 Chapter 2: Windows Configuration

need: check that unwanted inbound connections are blocked on both the private and public profiles
clues: green marks a protected profile and red marks an unprotected one
a user turned some protection off last week
the applet can be opened with a .cpl command
appliesWhen: inbound connections must be blocked or allowed, or a network profile's protection turned on or off, in the built-in host firewall
explanation: Windows Defender Firewall (firewall.cpl) shows the status of the private and public network profiles and turns protection on or off. It is the built-in host firewall that blocks unwanted inbound connections.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 36: Windows Control Panel Utilities

need: let one accounting program accept inbound connections on the private network
clues: the program is blocked by default
an Allow an app link meets the need
custom port rules are not needed
appliesWhen: inbound connections must be blocked or allowed, or a network profile's protection turned on or off, in the built-in host firewall
explanation: Windows Defender Firewall can allow an individual program through as an exception. Rules by port or address need the Advanced Security console instead.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 37: Windows Settings

need: create a second Outlook profile for a user who has two jobs
clues: the desktop version of Outlook is installed on the PC
the user wants to pick a profile each time Outlook starts
the server types and the account password must be entered
appliesWhen: Outlook profiles, accounts, or data files must be created or changed outside Outlook
explanation: The Mail applet appears only when Outlook is installed. It creates Outlook profiles, accounts, and data files, and it can make Outlook ask for a profile at startup.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Core 2 Chapter 2: Windows Configuration

need: add an extra Outlook data file to a profile while Outlook will not open
clues: the user's copy of Outlook crashes at startup
the profile must be changed from Control Panel
the applet is missing on PCs without Outlook
appliesWhen: Outlook profiles, accounts, or data files must be created or changed outside Outlook
explanation: The Mail applet changes Outlook profiles, accounts, and data files without starting Outlook. It shows in Control Panel only when Outlook is installed.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Core 2 Chapter 2: Windows Configuration

need: make a USB headset the default playback device
clues: the Playback tab lists both the speakers and the headset
the dialog opens with mmsys.cpl
a second microphone must also be set on the Recording tab
appliesWhen: playback or recording devices, the default device, or the communications volume behavior must be set
explanation: The Sound applet (mmsys.cpl) sets the default device on its Playback and Recording tabs. Right-clicking a device and selecting Set as default device makes the change.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 36: Windows Control Panel Utilities

need: lower the volume of other programs automatically during video calls
clues: the user joins many webinars
the option is on the Communications tab
the change must apply to all programs
appliesWhen: playback or recording devices, the default device, or the communications volume behavior must be set
explanation: The Communications tab of the Sound applet sets what Windows does with other audio when a call is detected. The same dialog also picks the playback and recording devices.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 36: Windows Control Panel Utilities

need: change an existing local user from administrator to standard
clues: the user is already set up on the PC
the UAC slider must also be raised
the help desk uses the classic Control Panel window
appliesWhen: an existing user's name or type, the UAC level, or saved credentials must be changed in Control Panel
explanation: User Accounts changes the name and type of an existing user and the User Account Control level. New users are created in Settings or in Local Users and Groups instead.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 36: Windows Control Panel Utilities

need: remove saved credentials and manage the file encryption certificate for the signed-in user
clues: the user changed a network share password
the old password is still stored
the classic Control Panel is the tool
appliesWhen: an existing user's name or type, the UAC level, or saved credentials must be changed in Control Panel
explanation: User Accounts links to the stored credentials and the file encryption certificates of the user. It also changes the user type and the UAC setting.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 36: Windows Control Panel Utilities

need: roll back a network adapter driver after an update
clues: the adapter stopped working after the new driver
the adapter shows a yellow exclamation mark
the console opens with devmgmt.msc
appliesWhen: a hardware driver must be updated, rolled back, or reinstalled, or a device enabled or disabled
explanation: Device Manager updates, rolls back, uninstalls, and disables device drivers. A yellow exclamation mark shows a device with a problem.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Core 2 Chapter 2: Windows Configuration

need: turn a webcam back on after someone switched it off in Windows
clues: the webcam no longer appears in any program
a down arrow in a circle marks the camera
the applet also opens with hdwwiz.cpl
appliesWhen: a hardware driver must be updated, rolled back, or reinstalled, or a device enabled or disabled
explanation: A down arrow in a circle in Device Manager marks a disabled device. Enabling the device there makes it work again.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Core 2 Chapter 2: Windows Configuration

need: make searches of a project folder on drive D return results faster
clues: the folder is not in the list of cataloged locations
the Modify button adds a location
adding the whole drive would slow the PC
appliesWhen: the locations or file types that Windows catalogs for fast searches must be changed, or the catalog rebuilt
explanation: Indexing Options lists the cataloged locations, and its Modify button adds or removes them. Searches of cataloged folders return results much faster.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 36: Windows Control Panel Utilities

need: rebuild the search catalog because searches miss files that exist
clues: the files are in a cataloged folder
the Advanced button holds the rebuild option
the file types that are covered may also change
appliesWhen: the locations or file types that Windows catalogs for fast searches must be changed, or the catalog rebuilt
explanation: The Advanced button in Indexing Options rebuilds the index, moves its storage location, and changes the file types that are cataloged.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 36: Windows Control Panel Utilities

need: reach Event Viewer, Task Scheduler, and Disk Cleanup from one Control Panel folder
clues: the folder holds shortcuts to many consoles
the local security policy editor must also be reachable
the folder has a new name in Windows 11
appliesWhen: the technician needs the Control Panel folder of shortcuts to consoles such as Event Viewer, Task Scheduler, and Local Security Policy
explanation: Administrative Tools, called Windows Tools in Windows 11, is a folder of shortcuts to consoles such as Event Viewer, Task Scheduler, and Disk Cleanup. Its tools share one theme: administering the operating system.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Core 2 Chapter 2: Windows Configuration

need: set up an iSCSI connection and run a memory diagnostic
clues: both tools are shortcuts in one Control Panel folder
the ODBC data sources tool sits in the same place
the technician does not want to search for each tool
appliesWhen: the technician needs the Control Panel folder of shortcuts to consoles such as Event Viewer, Task Scheduler, and Local Security Policy
explanation: The Administrative Tools folder (Windows Tools in Windows 11) holds the iSCSI Initiator, Windows Memory Diagnostic, and ODBC tools. Each item is a shortcut to an admin tool.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Core 2 Chapter 2: Windows Configuration

need: make each folder open in its own window and open items with a single click
clues: both options are on the General tab
the dialog also has View and Search tabs
the user wants the change for every folder
appliesWhen: folder browsing, click behavior, hidden items, file name extensions, or Quick access privacy must be changed
explanation: The General tab of File Explorer Options sets whether folders open in the same or a new window and whether a single or double click opens items. The View tab holds the hidden file and extension options.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 36: Windows Control Panel Utilities

need: show hidden items and file name extensions during a troubleshooting session
clues: both options are on the View tab
bootmgr and pagefile.sys must be visible
the change must apply to every folder
appliesWhen: folder browsing, click behavior, hidden items, file name extensions, or Quick access privacy must be changed
explanation: The View tab of File Explorer Options shows hidden files, shows extensions, and can unhide protected operating system files. These options are off by default so typical users see less.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 36: Windows Control Panel Utilities

need: stop recently used files and folders from showing in Quick access
clues: the user shares the PC with a coworker
the privacy options are on the General tab
the Clear button removes the history
appliesWhen: folder browsing, click behavior, hidden items, file name extensions, or Quick access privacy must be changed
explanation: The General tab of File Explorer Options has privacy check boxes that stop recent files and folders from showing in Quick access. Clearing them increases privacy on a shared PC.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 36: Windows Control Panel Utilities

need: make the High performance plan active and turn the display off after 15 minutes
clues: the applet opens with powercfg.cpl
the plan settings are changed with Change plan settings
the PC is a desktop on mains power
appliesWhen: a power plan, the power button or lid action, or advanced power settings must be set in Control Panel
explanation: Power Options (powercfg.cpl) selects or creates a power plan and sets when the display turns off. Its advanced settings also manage the drives, processor, and USB power.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 36: Windows Control Panel Utilities

need: set a docked laptop to keep running when its screen is folded shut
clues: the user works only on an external monitor
the Control Panel route is wanted
the power button action should stay the same
appliesWhen: a power plan, the power button or lid action, or advanced power settings must be set in Control Panel
explanation: Power Options has the Choose what closing the lid does and Choose what the power buttons do pages. Each can be set to Do nothing, Sleep, Hibernate, Shut down, or Turn off the display.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 36: Windows Control Panel Utilities

need: turn on the on-screen keyboard and the magnifier for a user with limited hand movement and low vision
clues: the user cannot press physical keys well
high contrast must also be offered
the matching Settings page opens with Windows+U
appliesWhen: the magnifier, Narrator, on-screen keyboard, or high contrast must be turned on for a user
explanation: Ease of Access Center turns on the magnifier, Narrator, the on-screen keyboard, and high contrast. Windows+U opens the matching accessibility page in Settings.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 36: Windows Control Panel Utilities

need: have the screen read aloud for a user who is blind
clues: voice prompts must describe each window
the help desk uses the classic Control Panel
the user may also need high contrast
appliesWhen: the magnifier, Narrator, on-screen keyboard, or high contrast must be turned on for a user
explanation: Ease of Access Center turns on Narrator, which reads the screen aloud with voice prompts. The same center turns on the magnifier, the on-screen keyboard, and high contrast.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 36: Windows Control Panel Utilities

need: see the AppData folder in a user's profile folder
clues: the folder does not appear in File Explorer
the folder has the hidden attribute
protected operating system files do not need to be seen

answer.item: Show hidden files, folders, and drives

appliesWhen: items that have the hidden attribute must appear in File Explorer
explanation: Hidden items are not shown by default. Selecting Show hidden files, folders, and drives on the View tab of File Explorer Options makes them appear.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 36: Windows Control Panel Utilities

need: make bootmgr visible in the root of drive C
clues: hidden items are already shown
the file is marked as an operating system file
a warning appears before the change is saved
appliesWhen: files that Windows marks as protected must appear, by clearing that check box
explanation: Files such as bootmgr and pagefile.sys stay out of sight until the Hide protected operating system files check box is cleared. Showing hidden items alone is not enough.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 36: Windows Control Panel Utilities

need: see whether a file named invoice.pdf is really a program
clues: the file looks like a document in File Explorer
the part of the name after the last dot is not shown
the option is a check box on the View tab

answer.item: Hide extensions for known file types

appliesWhen: file name extensions must be shown or hidden, by clearing or checking that box
explanation: Windows hides extensions for known file types by default. Clearing that check box shows the full name, so a file ending in .exe can be spotted.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 36: Windows Control Panel Utilities

need: keep the parent folder in view when a subfolder is opened
clues: the user compares two folders side by side
the option is on the General tab
folders now replace each other in one window

answer.item: Open each folder in its own window

appliesWhen: every opened folder must get a new window instead of using the same one
explanation: By default each folder opens in the same window. The General tab can open each folder in its own window instead, which can leave many windows open.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 36: Windows Control Panel Utilities

need: shorten the boot time of an older PC with a mechanical hard drive
clues: the user shuts the PC down every night
the kernel and drivers can be saved to disk at shutdown
the option is under the shutdown settings of the power button page
appliesWhen: boot time after a full shutdown must be shorter, by saving the kernel to disk
explanation: Fast startup saves the kernel and drivers to disk at shutdown, as hibernation does but without the user session. At power-on Windows loads that saved kernel, which helps slow machines most.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 37: Windows Settings

need: save battery by cutting power to idle USB devices
clues: the laptop runs on battery all day
the option is in the advanced power settings
devices in use must keep working

a little power use is acceptable

explanation: A manual proxy setting sends all web requests to the proxy server, so pages fail when that server cannot be reached. Other IP traffic still works.

clues: no updates have downloaded for weeks
the laptop now uses only the office Wi-Fi
a former user often worked from a phone hotspot
the user has no data limit on the office network

answer.cause: the Wi-Fi connection is marked as metered, so large downloads are held back
answer.action: Turn off the metered connection setting for the office Wi-Fi

appliesWhen: a connection with no data cap is still marked as metered
explanation: Windows limits data use on a metered connection, so large downloads such as updates are held back. The office network has no cap, so it should not be metered.

clues: the option to join a domain is missing
the PC is a new consumer laptop from a retail store
other office PCs joined the domain without problems
the domain name and credentials are correct

answer.cause: the PC runs Windows Home, which cannot join a domain
answer.action: Upgrade the PC to Windows Pro and then join the domain

appliesWhen: the edition of Windows does not support joining an Active Directory domain
explanation: Home editions of Windows cannot connect to Active Directory. The PC needs an edition such as Pro before it can join the domain.

need: install an application into a new virtual machine that has no optical drive

the virtual machine has no physical drive
the install must run as if from the original disc
the hypervisor can attach image files

answer.item: Mounting the ISO image of the installation disc

appliesWhen: the install files come as a disc image that can be attached
explanation: An ISO image is one file that holds everything on an optical disc. A hypervisor or Windows can mount it as a drive, which is faster than a physical disc.

need: set up 40 new PCs with the same operating system, apps, and settings
clues: every PC needs the same app suite
a reference PC is already set up and prepared with sysprep
the PCs have no user data yet
the rollout must be fast and consistent

answer.item: Deploying a prepared system image to every PC

appliesWhen: many identical new computers need the same OS and software
explanation: An image holds an operating system with all its software already installed. After sysprep prepares it, the same image can be deployed to many PCs much faster than separate installs.

need: install one app on a home PC after buying it online
clues: the vendor sells the app from its website
no disc or USB drive came with the purchase
the PC has a fast internet connection
only one PC needs the app

answer.item: Downloading the installer package from the vendor

appliesWhen: the app is bought online and installed on a single computer
explanation: Most apps are now sold as downloadable packages that are run through the installer. Online stores can even install the app from a digital library.

need: install a licensed app on one PC in a lab that is never connected to the internet
clues: the lab PC has no internet connection by policy
the vendor shipped the app on a DVD
only one PC needs the app
the PC has an optical drive

answer.item: Installing from the vendor's physical installation disc

appliesWhen: a single offline computer must install from the media the vendor shipped
explanation: Physical media works for a one-off install on a computer with no network access. It is slow and does not scale well when many PCs need the app.

need: install an app on 25 PCs that are already in use and must keep their user data
clues: the installer files can be placed on the file server
the PCs already hold user data and settings
each install is started by a technician
the office network is fast

answer.item: Running the installer from a read-only network share

appliesWhen: many existing computers must install an app from a central location
explanation: A network installation puts the installer on a share with read-only access so many PCs can install at the same time. It keeps each PC's existing data, unlike a new image.

need: run a 3D design program that lists 4 GB of video memory as a requirement
clues: the PC has integrated graphics that share system RAM
the program needs hardware acceleration
the motherboard has a free PCIe x16 slot
the CPU and RAM already meet the requirements

answer.item: Installing a dedicated graphics card with enough VRAM

appliesWhen: an app needs more video memory or graphics power than integrated graphics give
explanation: Integrated graphics share system RAM and are much slower. A dedicated card in a PCIe slot has its own fast VRAM for graphics-heavy programs.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 1: Operating System Basics

need: run an app that the vendor offers only as a 64-bit program
clues: the CPU supports x64
the installed copy of Windows 10 is 32-bit
the installer will not run on this PC
the PC has 8 GB of RAM

answer.item: Reinstalling the PC with a 64-bit edition of Windows

appliesWhen: a 64-bit CPU runs a 32-bit OS that cannot run 64-bit software
explanation: A 32-bit operating system cannot run 64-bit software, even on a 64-bit CPU. A 64-bit edition of Windows runs both 64-bit and 32-bit apps.

need: check that a new multiuser app will not open ports or conflict with other software before the rollout
clues: the app will run on every PC in the company
a bad app could bring down systems and cause lost revenue
nobody has used the app in this environment
an evaluation version is available

answer.item: Testing the app on an isolated test network or virtual machines first

appliesWhen: a new app must be checked for security and conflicts before it reaches live PCs
explanation: Each new app adds to the attack surface and can open ports or conflict with other programs. Testing on an isolated testbed finds these issues before live clients are affected.

need: find out whether the network can handle a new video chat app for 80 staff
clues: every staff member will stream video at the same time
other users already complain about slow file transfers
the switches are several years old
the app vendor publishes the data rate for each call

answer.item: Comparing the app's per-user bandwidth with the network's capacity

appliesWhen: the impact of a new app on the network must be judged before it is installed
explanation: Streaming apps can use a large share of the network and slow down other users. The bandwidth each user needs, times the number of users, must fit the network's capacity.

the app worked yesterday on the same laptop
the vendor licenses the app with a USB dongle
the user worked from home this morning

appliesWhen: the app's license depends on a USB hardware token that is missing
explanation: Some apps check for a USB hardware token every time they run. Without the token plugged in, the app cannot find its license.

the OS and RAM meet the requirements

explanation: The storage requirement is a minimum, and close is not good enough. Unused apps can be removed under Settings > Apps to free the space.

the vendor no longer updates the program

explanation: Application compatibility lets an old program behave as if it runs on an older Windows version. It handles programs that expect looser file and Registry permissions.

clues: the installer says the app cannot run on this PC

the system information shows an x86-based operating system
the CPU is a modern 64-bit model

explanation: A 32-bit operating system cannot run 64-bit software, even when the CPU supports 64-bit. A 64-bit Windows runs both kinds of apps.

explanation: An app that logs all the time can fill the drive and slow other programs with disk activity. The impact on the device should be checked after a new app is installed.

the old mail client needed server addresses typed into each PC
nothing should be installed on the shared PCs
users already have multifactor sign-in

appliesWhen: users need email anywhere with only a sign-in and a browser
explanation: Web-based email such as Gmail or Outlook on the web is software as a service. Users only sign in, so there are no server settings to enter and mail works from any device.

the user is often without an internet connection
messages written offline must send when the connection returns
a recent year of mail must be searchable offline

explanation: Cached Exchange Mode downloads recent mail, 12 months by default, to the computer. New messages wait in the Outbox until the internet connection returns.

need: keep copies of a user's Desktop and Documents folders in cloud storage automatically

the user often forgets to back up files
the files must be the same on the laptop and the desktop
a lost laptop must not mean lost work

answer.item: OneDrive folder sync for the Desktop and Documents folders

explanation: OneDrive syncs chosen local folders with cloud storage, so files saved locally are uploaded and files added online come down. Its settings let the user choose which folders sync.

need: show every cloud file in File Explorer without filling a small laptop drive

the cloud library holds 400 GB
the user opens only a few files each day
the files are stored in OneDrive

explanation: Files On-Demand shows cloud files as placeholders that download only when they are opened. That saves local disk space while every file still appears in File Explorer.

the staff work from different locations
edits must show in real time

explanation: Cloud spreadsheets such as Excel online or Google Sheets live in one online copy. Several users can edit at the same time and always see the latest version.

there is no dedicated meeting room hardware
everyone has a webcam and broadband
the meeting needs live audio and screen sharing

explanation: Cloud videoconferencing tools such as Teams, Zoom, or Google Meet need only ordinary hardware and broadband. They give live video, audio, and screen sharing to remote teams.

the former employee's account still holds a license
